question: Across finite clock arrivals and heterogeneous request lengths, does admission cap2 with a current-decode-aware prefill rule improve complete-request tradeoffs beyond static cap3 and static cap2?
hypothesis: Native admission changes concurrency and transfer amortization; releasing prefill to budget64 only when no decode is ready may use an idle decode phase. Request queueing, submit lag, payload and completion must all be charged.
selection_scope: Next contiguous eight source entries after previously used paging calibration sources0..11, selected before GPU outcome. Existing project public articles, not a globally untouched dataset. Short prefixes are controlled inputs, not complete-article or production traffic evidence.
ordering: A,B,C,C,B,A; six independent engine processes. Two observations per arm; no randomized independent blocks or statistical significance claimed.
action: A cap3/static32, B cap2/static32, C cap2 with threshold32 if any current running decode is ready else threshold0 (native total budget64). No future routes/output length oracle; all existing decode must advance. All requests arrive by the declared clock and are submitted at synchronous step boundaries.
accounting: TTFT = declared arrival to submission + submission to first schedule + first schedule to first token. Synchronous submit lag remains charged. Cohort wall contains all queueing and idle intervals; do not add waiting again. Host/GPU spans may overlap. Weight tensor-copy payload is not PCIe wire bytes.
required_checks: 8 completed requests and264 outputs per cell
672 prefill positions plus256 decode positions,928 scheduled rows
every ready decode scheduled exactly once, no preemption
actual cap and phase threshold applied before native.schedule
threshold0 and actual per-request prefill above32 reported separately
all attempts/repeats and whole parent/engine cycles retained
comparison: C vs B is the phase-rule residual; B vs A is ordinary admission. Also C vs A and each same-arm repeat. Cross-arm outputs/routes need not match; no fixed-route counterfactual. Observed drift is not a noise bound; no post-hoc SLO or arbitrary percent GO gate.
claim_ceiling: Exploratory native-serving request tradeoffs on OLMoE with artificial expert budget and one finite clock episode. Not production tail latency, sustained arrival capacity, quality equivalence, true over-HBM deployment, novel method or statistical noninferiority.
lifecycle: Common source/field check and nested observation before both warmups, pager reset before measurement. Each cell owns a fresh engine; capture restores schedule callable, cap/threshold persist to engine shutdown. No cross-cell engine reuse.
continuation: If phase has a complete-cost residual beyond both ordinary statics, qualify on another independently selected arrival episode; if not, identify whether admission delay, absent action or extra transfers closes it and stop this rule in the covered regime. Do not tune the evaluated episode or revive RR/one8.
stops: GPU query failure/foreign process, source/input mismatch, missing request/position, dropped ready decode, unsupported async/spec/preemption, or accounting failure stops and retains the campaign; no retry/reorder based on performance.
